sections.title: Sex and Education
sections.description: Despite recurring efforts to exclude recognitions of sexuality from formal educational contexts, schools operate as contested yet generative sites for discourses on sexual identities, practices, and politics. This course will explore how cultural anxieties, political debates, and competing pedagogical aims around sexuality have shaped policies, practices, and participation in both K-12 and post-secondary educational settings. Topics will include the sociosexual construction of the child, the surveillance of youth and adult sexualities in schools, battles over and approaches to sex education, the struggle for LGBTQ+ inclusion, the intersections of race, region, sexuality, and schooling, and the liberatory potential of critical pedagogies of sexuality.
